note: SRS requirements are from INSYS Core SRS v1.0 (21 Oct 2026). SDM and DBA requirements are proposed in the companion specifications, not SRS requirements.

srs.BIL-001: The platform MUST generate billing obligations from authorised policy and premium transactions.
srs.BIL-002: Billing records MUST reference the source policy, tenant, product, currency, and relevant business dates.
srs.BIL-003: The system MUST support partial payments and payment allocation according to configured rules.
srs.BIL-004: The platform MUST maintain an auditable history of billing adjustments and reversals.
srs.CLM-001: All domains MUST use shared claims infrastructure where the capabilities are genuinely common.
srs.CLM-002: Each domain MUST own its claims adjudication logic.
srs.CLM-003: Claim decisions MUST record the relevant policy or coverage references, decision rationale, evidence references, applicable rules, authority, and timestamps.
srs.CLM-004: Claims reserves, approved amounts, payments, and recoveries MUST be represented as traceable financial movements.
srs.CLM-005: Claims processing MUST safely handle duplicate submissions and retry scenarios.
srs.DOC-001: Documents MUST be tenant-scoped and access-controlled.
srs.DOC-002: Generated documents MUST retain references to the applicable template and product versions.
srs.DOC-003: Access to sensitive documents MUST be auditable.
srs.DOC-004: Medical and other highly sensitive documents MUST receive additional access controls appropriate to their classification.
srs.DST-001: Intermediaries MUST have controlled records and configurable product permissions.
srs.DST-002: Commission rules MUST support effective dating and versioning.
srs.DST-003: Commission calculations MUST retain the applicable plan version and source transaction.
srs.DST-004: Commission payments MUST be subject to appropriate approval and financial controls.
srs.FIN-001: Financial transactions MUST be traceable to their originating business transactions.
srs.FIN-002: Posted entries MUST NOT be silently overwritten.
srs.FIN-003: Corrections MUST use explicit reversal or adjustment transactions.
srs.FIN-004: Posting rules and account mappings MUST be versioned and governed.
srs.FIN-005: The subledger MUST support tenant, currency, accounting date, transaction date, source domain, and business reference as applicable.
srs.FIN-006: Financial reconciliation MUST identify unmatched, duplicated, delayed, and inconsistent transactions.
srs.FIN-007: Integration failures MUST be visible to authorised operational users.
srs.GEN-001: The domain MUST support quotation, underwriting, and policy issuance.
srs.GEN-002: Policies MUST support multiple insured risk objects where applicable.
srs.GEN-003: Endorsements MUST support effective dates, coverage changes, premium adjustments, document generation, and audit history.
srs.GEN-004: Renewals, cancellations, and reinstatements MUST follow configurable product rules.
srs.GEN-005: Different product families MUST be able to use distinct risk attributes and rating logic.
srs.GEN-006: Claims MUST support registration, coverage validation, assessment, reserves, approval, settlement, and closure.
srs.GEN-007: The system SHOULD support loss adjusters, surveyors, repairers, salvage, and third-party recovery.
srs.GEN-008: Claim settlement MUST account for deductibles, excesses, limits, and applicable valuation rules.
srs.HLT-001: The domain MUST support health products, plans, benefits, exclusions, waiting periods, co-payments, and limits.
srs.HLT-002: The domain MUST support principal members, dependants, group schemes, enrolment, and membership lifecycle changes.
srs.HLT-003: The platform MUST expose authorised member-eligibility inquiries.
srs.HLT-004: Provider contracts and tariffs MUST support effective dating.
srs.HLT-005: The platform MUST support preauthorisation requests, decisions, limits, expiry, and audit.
srs.HLT-006: The domain MUST support provider-submitted claims and member reimbursement claims.
srs.HLT-007: Medical claims MUST validate membership, coverage, benefit limits, applicable tariffs, preauthorisation, and configured exclusions.
srs.HLT-008: Medical information MUST be restricted according to role, purpose, and minimum necessary access.
srs.HLT-009: Provider and member payments MUST be traceable and reconcilable.
srs.IAM-001: The platform MUST support tenant-scoped user identities and permissions.
srs.IAM-002: It MUST support federation with approved identity providers using standard protocols such as OpenID Connect or SAML where required.
srs.IAM-003: Multi-factor authentication MUST be supported for privileged and sensitive roles.
srs.IAM-004: Service accounts MUST have explicit scopes, limited permissions, and controlled credentials.
srs.IAM-005: The system MUST support prompt revocation of compromised or deactivated identities.
srs.IAM-006: Sensitive operations MUST record the acting user or service identity, tenant, operation, target resource, timestamp, and outcome.
srs.IAM-007: Authorisation MUST be enforced by backend services and MUST NOT rely exclusively on user-interface restrictions.
srs.INT-001: APIs MUST be documented and versioned.
srs.INT-002: APIs MUST enforce authentication, authorisation, tenant scope, and input validation.
srs.INT-003: Non-repeatable business operations MUST support idempotency where appropriate.
srs.INT-004: Events MUST have stable identifiers and versioned schemas.
srs.INT-005: Event consumers MUST tolerate duplicate delivery.
srs.INT-006: Failed integrations MUST support controlled retry, monitoring, and recovery.
srs.INT-007: Event payloads MUST minimise sensitive data.
srs.LIF-001: The domain MUST support proposal capture and quotation.
srs.LIF-002: Underwriting decisions MUST be traceable and reproducible to the extent permitted by retained data and calculation methods.
srs.LIF-003: Issued policies MUST reference approved product and configuration versions.
srs.LIF-004: Policy servicing MUST validate each requested change against policy state, product rules, and applicable authority.
srs.LIF-005: Premium processing MUST support configured payment frequencies, grace periods, arrears, lapse, and reinstatement.
srs.LIF-006: The domain MUST support product-appropriate death, disability, critical illness, maturity, and other benefit claims.
srs.LIF-007: Cash-value, surrender-value, and loan capabilities MUST be enabled only for products that support them.
srs.LIF-008: Life claims MUST validate policy status, insured-life details, benefit eligibility, exclusions, and claimant authority.
srs.NFR-001: Availability: 99.9% monthly availability for core production services (proposed starting target, not a contractual commitment)
srs.NFR-002: Standard API latency: p95 ≤ 2 s for agreed standard operations under benchmark load (proposed starting target, not a contractual commitment)
srs.NFR-003: Standard rating latency: p95 ≤ 3 s for agreed standard rating scenarios (proposed starting target, not a contractual commitment)
srs.NFR-004: Scalability: Horizontal scaling for stateless and high-volume components (proposed starting target, not a contractual commitment)
srs.NFR-005: Recovery Point Objective: RPO ≤ 15 minutes for core transactional data (proposed starting target, not a contractual commitment)
srs.NFR-006: Recovery Time Objective: RTO ≤ 4 hours for a regional disaster scenario (proposed starting target, not a contractual commitment)
srs.NFR-007: Auditability: End-to-end traceability for critical policy, claim, configuration and financial operations (proposed starting target, not a contractual commitment)
srs.NFR-008: Maintainability: Documented interfaces, automated tests, clear ownership (proposed starting target, not a contractual commitment)
srs.NFR-009: Interoperability: Versioned APIs and governed integration contracts (proposed starting target, not a contractual commitment)
srs.NFR-010: Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA for web interfaces where applicable (proposed starting target, not a contractual commitment)
srs.NFR-011: Portability: Automated deployment, limited dependence on cloud-specific services (proposed starting target, not a contractual commitment)
srs.NFR-012: Observability: Centralised metrics, logs, traces, dashboards and alerts (proposed starting target, not a contractual commitment)
srs.NFR-013: Data integrity: Domain invariants enforced within authoritative transactional boundaries (proposed starting target, not a contractual commitment)
srs.NFR-014: Backup: Encrypted, monitored, access-controlled, restore-tested backups (proposed starting target, not a contractual commitment)
srs.NFR-015: Capacity: Load tests for peak quotes, issuance, claims, provider submissions, month-end (proposed starting target, not a contractual commitment)
srs.PAY-001: Payment operations MUST use idempotency controls to prevent duplicate financial effects.
srs.PAY-002: Payment status changes MUST be traceable.
srs.PAY-003: The system MUST support reconciliation between internal transactions and external bank or payment-provider records.
srs.PAY-004: Payment credentials and sensitive payment data MUST be protected.
srs.PAY-005: Failed or ambiguous payments MUST enter a controlled exception or reconciliation process rather than being silently treated as successful.
srs.PRD-002: Published product versions MUST be immutable.
srs.PRD-003: Changes to published products MUST create a new version.
srs.PRD-004: The system MUST validate product configuration before publication.
srs.PRD-005: The platform MUST support simulation and test cases before publication.
srs.PRD-007: Product versions MUST support effective dates.
srs.PRD-008: Transactions MUST retain references to the product, rating, and rules versions used.
srs.PRD-009: The system MUST identify missing parameters, invalid values, incompatible benefits, and unresolved dependencies.
srs.PTY-001: The system MUST support individuals and organisations.
srs.PTY-002: A party MUST be capable of holding multiple roles.
srs.PTY-003: The system MUST support tenant-scoped party access and controlled sharing of information.
srs.PTY-004: Duplicate detection and record merging SHOULD be supported with an auditable history.
srs.PTY-005: Personal information MUST be collected and exposed according to authorised business purposes and applicable privacy requirements.
srs.REI-001: Reinsurance records MUST retain links to the underlying policies, risks, claims, and financial transactions.
srs.REI-002: Cession calculations MUST be reproducible using the applicable arrangement and configuration versions.
srs.REI-003: Reinsurance recoverables and settlements MUST be traceable and reconcilable.
srs.SRS-001: The platform MUST support configurable role-based access control.
srs.SRS-002: The platform MUST support configurable maker-checker controls for sensitive operations, including product publication, underwriting overrides, claim approval, payment release, financial adjustments and privileged user administration.
srs.SRS-003: Permissions MUST be restricted to authorised tenants and, where configured, to specific products, branches, organisations, and transaction categories.
srs.TEN-001: Every tenant MUST have a unique, immutable identifier.
srs.TEN-002: Tenant context MUST be derived from a trusted authentication or service identity mechanism. An untrusted request parameter alone MUST NOT determine the tenant.
srs.TEN-003: Every tenant-scoped operation MUST validate that the authenticated principal is authorised for the resolved tenant.
srs.TEN-004: The platform MUST enforce tenant isolation across transactional data, documents, APIs, caches, events, search, analytics, reporting, and background processing.
srs.TEN-005: Cross-tenant access attempts MUST be rejected and logged.
srs.TEN-006: Tenant-specific product configurations, user permissions, integration credentials, and operational settings MUST remain isolated.
srs.TEN-007: Administrative access to tenant data MUST be controlled, auditable, and restricted to an approved operational purpose.
srs.TEN-008: Tenant onboarding, suspension, reactivation, and termination MUST be governed by defined workflows.
srs.WFL-002: A workflow transition MUST invoke the owning domain’s business validation.
srs.WFL-003: Workflows MUST support assignment, reassignment, escalation, and controlled delegation.
srs.WFL-004: Sensitive transitions MUST enforce approval authority.
srs.WFL-005: Long-running workflows MUST support recovery after service restarts or temporary integration failures.

SDM-001.text: Every static data entity is registered in a catalogue with owner role, class, scope, tier and data classification.

SDM-002.text: Business codes are immutable after first activation. A change in meaning creates a new code or a new version.

SDM-003.text: Tier 1 changes require maker-checker approval by a different user. Tier 2 changes require it unless the tenant switches it off.

SDM-004.text: All Tier 1 and Tier 2 items are effective-dated. Future-dated changes are allowed. Effective periods for one code must not overlap.

SDM-005.text: Retroactive changes to active Tier 1 data are prohibited except through an approved correction workflow with an impact report.

SDM-006.text: Transactions keep the version of every Tier 1 item that governed them, so results can be reproduced.

SDM-007.text: A referenced code cannot be deleted. It can only be deprecated or retired, with a replacement mapping where needed.

SDM-008.text: Tenant data is isolated. A tenant overlay never changes a platform-global baseline.

SDM-009.text: Each activated change publishes a versioned event carrying the tenant ID. Consumers invalidate tenant-aware caches on receipt.

SDM-010.text: Before activation, Tier 1 changes show their impact: affected products, policies in force, open claims and scheduled runs.

SDM-011.text: Rating, rules, posting and cession changes are simulated against approved test cases before activation.

SDM-012.text: Bulk imports are fully validated before commit. Each batch commits completely or not at all, and rejected lines are reported individually.

SDM-013.text: Data quality rules (mandatory fields, ranges, cross-references, overlapping periods) are enforced on save and again on approval.

SDM-014.text: Every change is audited with actor, tenant, before and after values, reason, time and outcome.

SDM-015.text: Any static data set can be queried and exported as at a past date for audit and dispute resolution.

SDM-016.text: Secret values are never stored as static data. Records hold only references to the secrets manager.

SDM-017.text: Confidential master data such as bank details is masked by default, and each unmasked view is audited.

SDM-018.text: External standard lists record their source, edition and load date. Updates pass through the same approval as internal changes.

SDM-019.text: Labels support multiple languages, with a tenant-level fallback language.

SDM-020.text: Static data moves between environments only through an approved, audited configuration package.

DBA-001.text: Every tenant-scoped table has tenant_id NOT NULL as the first primary key column.

DBA-002.text: Row-level security is enabled and forced on every tenant-scoped table. Application roles never own tables and never hold BYPASSRLS.

DBA-003.text: The tenant for a transaction is set only from the authenticated principal, never from request input. If it is missing, queries fail.

DBA-004.text: Each module owns one schema. Only its service role has write privileges on it.

DBA-005.text: No foreign keys cross module schemas. Cross-module references are plain IDs, checked through APIs or events.

DBA-006.text: Each module writes domain events to its own outbox table in the same transaction as the business change.

DBA-007.text: Each consumer records processed event IDs under a unique key and ignores duplicates.

DBA-008.text: Non-repeatable operations store an idempotency key, request hash and original response.

DBA-009.text: Posted financial records are insert-only. Service roles have no UPDATE or DELETE on them, and corrections are reversal rows.

DBA-010.text: Transactions store the version of each configuration item that governed them.

DBA-011.text: Mutable rows use optimistic concurrency through row_version.

DBA-012.text: Money is stored as numeric with an explicit currency column. Floating-point types are not used for money or rates.

DBA-013.text: Timestamps are timestamptz in UTC. Business dates such as accounting and effective dates are plain dates.

DBA-014.text: Highly sensitive identifiers are encrypted by the application, with a keyed hash for exact-match lookup.

DBA-015.text: Medical columns are reachable only through column-level grants and purpose-specific views.

DBA-016.text: The audit table is insert-only, partitioned by month and retained per the audit retention policy.

DBA-017.text: Schema changes are versioned, forward-only migrations applied by the pipeline. Manual DDL in production is not allowed.

DBA-018.text: High-volume append-only tables are partitioned by time, with the partition key in the primary key.

DBA-019.text: Reporting and analytics read from replicas or projections, never from transactional primaries.

DBA-020.text: Backups are encrypted, monitored and restore-tested. Profiles B and C support per-tenant restore.

DBA-021.text: Transactional records are never soft-deleted. They change status, and history is kept in log or event tables.

DBA-022.text: When retention ends, personal data is anonymised in place so financial totals and audit evidence stay intact.

DBA-023.text: Every partition carries the same row-level security policy as its parent, and partitions are created ahead of need. A row with no matching partition is rejected.
